findings.requirement: Decision W8: Every PUT carries the attribution headers from the existing HostAuditGateway (invocation ID, approver, reasoning hash). The proposal stores the approval and rollback audit records (who and when).
findings.finding: Rollback PUT requests to Frappe do not carry HostAuditGateway attribution headers and the service fails to record the rollback audit envelope on the proposal.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/writeback/service.py:182-185, rollback calls await self._call(auth.tenant_id, lambda c: c.update_document(proposal['doctype'], proposal['name'], proposal['before'])) without headers, unlike approve() at lines 158-167. In Frappe mock PUT logs, frappe.puts[-1]['headers'] contains zero x-* tracing headers during rollback, and proposal['audit'] retains only approve headers while rollback audit records are never stored.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c "import asyncio, httpx, yaml, os, tempfile; from tests.unit.test_writeback import StatefulFrappe, PROPOSER, APPROVER, HOSTS; from hrms_plugin.writeback.service import WritebackService; from hrms_plugin.storage.memory_store import MemoryKeyValueStore; from hrms_plugin.integrations.frappe import FrappeClient; f = StatefulFrappe(); svc = WritebackService(MemoryKeyValueStore(), lambda h,k,s: FrappeClient(h,k,s,http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(f.handler)))); os.environ['ACME_FRAPPE_KEY']='k'; os.environ['ACME_FRAPPE_SECRET']='s'; tf = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', delete=False); yaml.safe_dump(HOSTS, tf); os.environ['HRMS_HOSTS']=tf.name; p = asyncio.run(svc.propose(PROPOSER, 'Employee', 'HR-EMP-00001', {'notice_number_of_days': 60})); asyncio.run(svc.approve(APPROVER, p['id'])); asyncio.run(svc.rollback(APPROVER, p['id'])); assert 'x-hitl-approver-id' not in f.puts[-1]['headers'], 'Attribution headers unexpectedly present'"

findings.requirement: Decision W4: Patch validation: at least one field; every field allowlisted; values type-checked (int excludes bool; date is a valid YYYY-MM-DD; string <= 140 chars; decimal is a finite decimal string). A patch equal to the current values -> NO_CHANGE.
findings.finding: Decimal patch equality comparison compares raw string against host numeric float or integer, preventing NO_CHANGE detection and falsely allowing redundant writes.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/writeback/service.py:118-121, diff = [{'field': f, 'before': document.get(f), 'after': v} for f, v in sorted(patch.items()) if document.get(f) != v]. Decimal patches require str (e.g. '1500.5') while Frappe returns JSON float or integer (e.g. 1500.5). In Python 1500.5 != '1500.5' evaluates to True, so NO_CHANGE is never raised when proposing an identical decimal value.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c "import asyncio, httpx, yaml, os, tempfile; from tests.unit.test_writeback import PROPOSER; from hrms_plugin.writeback.service import WritebackService; from hrms_plugin.storage.memory_store import MemoryKeyValueStore; from hrms_plugin.integrations.frappe import FrappeClient; hosts={'tenants': [{'tenant_id': 'acme', 'vendor': 'frappe', 'base_url': 'https://hr.acme.test', 'api_key_env': 'K', 'api_secret_env': 'S', 'timeout_seconds': 10, 'writable_fields': {'Employee': {'rate': 'decimal'}}}]}; os.environ['K']='k'; os.environ['S']='s'; tf = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', delete=False); yaml.safe_dump(hosts, tf); os.environ['HRMS_HOSTS']=tf.name; doc={'name':'HR-EMP-00001','rate':1500.5,'modified':'2026-10-01 10:00:00.000001'}; h = lambda r: httpx.Response(200, json={'data': doc}); svc = WritebackService(MemoryKeyValueStore(), lambda h,k,s: FrappeClient(h,k,s,http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(h)))); p = asyncio.run(svc.propose(PROPOSER, 'Employee', 'HR-EMP-00001', {'rate': '1500.5'})); assert len(p['diff']) == 1 and p['diff'][0]['before'] == 1500.5, 'Expected false positive diff'"

findings.finding: Frappe Employee standard identifier field middle_name is absent from _FIELD_KINDS, allowing it to be configured as a writable field without triggering host registry rejection.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/security/pii.py:155-157, _FIELD_KINDS defines name, first_name, last_name, full_name, employee_name, candidate_name but omits middle_name. identifier_kind('middle_name') returns None. HostConfig._no_pii_writes in hrms_plugin/integrations/host_registry.py:48-52 fails to reject writable_fields configuring middle_name.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c "from hrms_plugin.security.pii import identifier_kind; from hrms_plugin.integrations.host_registry import load_host_registry; import tempfile, yaml; assert identifier_kind('middle_name') is None; data={'tenants': [{'tenant_id': 'acme', 'vendor': 'frappe', 'base_url': 'https://hr.acme.test', 'api_key_env': 'K', 'api_secret_env': 'S', 'timeout_seconds': 10, 'writable_fields': {'Employee': {'middle_name': 'string'}}}]}; tf = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', delete=False); yaml.safe_dump(data, tf); reg = load_host_registry(tf.name); assert 'Employee' in reg.for_tenant('acme').writable_fields"

findings.requirement: Decision W5: Concurrency (our own, since Frappe documents none): ... On rollback, re-read; if modified != the modified returned by our write -> ROLLBACK_CONFLICT and nothing is written.
findings.finding: Approve does not validate that after_modified returned by the host update is a valid timestamp, permanently breaking rollback if the host response omits modified.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/writeback/service.py:168, proposal.update(status='EXECUTED', after_modified=updated.get('modified'), ...) records after_modified without ensuring it is a non-empty string (unlike propose() at lines 115-117). If the host omits modified, after_modified is saved as None, causing rollback() at line 180 (current.get('modified') != proposal.get('after_modified')) to perpetually raise ROLLBACK_CONFLICT.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c "import asyncio, httpx, yaml, os, tempfile; from tests.unit.test_writeback import PROPOSER, APPROVER, HOSTS; from hrms_plugin.writeback.service import WritebackService, WritebackError; from hrms_plugin.storage.memory_store import MemoryKeyValueStore; from hrms_plugin.integrations.frappe import FrappeClient; doc={'name':'HR-EMP-00001','notice_number_of_days':30,'modified':'2026-10-01 10:00:00.000001'}; async def h(r): return httpx.Response(200, json={'data': {'name': 'HR-EMP-00001', 'notice_number_of_days': 60}}) if r.method=='PUT' else httpx.Response(200, json={'data': dict(doc)}); svc = WritebackService(MemoryKeyValueStore(), lambda h,k,s: FrappeClient(h,k,s,http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(h)))); os.environ['ACME_FRAPPE_KEY']='k'; os.environ['ACME_FRAPPE_SECRET']='s'; tf = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', delete=False); yaml.safe_dump(HOSTS, tf); os.environ['HRMS_HOSTS']=tf.name; p = asyncio.run(svc.propose(PROPOSER, 'Employee', 'HR-EMP-00001', {'notice_number_of_days': 60})); asyncio.run(svc.approve(APPROVER, p['id'])); import pytest; pytest.raises(WritebackError, asyncio.run, svc.rollback(APPROVER, p['id']))"

findings.requirement: Decision W11: HTTP mapping: NOT_FOUND 404; FIELD_NOT_WRITABLE / INVALID_VALUE / NO_CHANGE 422; CONFLICT / ROLLBACK_CONFLICT / EXPIRED / INVALID_STATE 409; SAME_PERSON 403; HOST_NOT_CONFIGURED 503; HOST_ERROR 502.
findings.finding: Writeback service discards host exception diagnostic details by passing exc.code instead of exc.detail to WritebackError.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/writeback/service.py:86-87, except FrappeError as exc: raise WritebackError('HOST_ERROR', exc.code) from None passes exc.code (which is the literal string 'HOST_ERROR') instead of exc.detail (e.g. 'HTTPStatusError: 502'). This renders redundant error payloads {'error': 'HOST_ERROR', 'detail': 'HOST_ERROR'}.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c "from hrms_plugin.integrations.frappe import FrappeError; from hrms_plugin.writeback.service import WritebackError; exc = FrappeError('HOST_ERROR', 'HTTPStatusError: 502'); wb = WritebackError('HOST_ERROR', exc.code); assert wb.detail == 'HOST_ERROR' and wb.detail != exc.detail"

findings.requirement: Decision W8: Every PUT carries the attribution headers from the existing HostAuditGateway (invocation ID, approver, reasoning hash).
findings.finding: Rollback test asserts body payload restoration but fails to assert attribution headers on the host PUT, allowing the rollback audit header omission to pass unnoticed.
findings.evidence: In tests/unit/test_writeback.py:195-202, test_rollback_restores_before_values_once checks assert frappe.puts[-1]['body'] == {'notice_number_of_days': 30} and idempotency, but unlike test_approve_writes_once_with_audit_headers (lines 142-144) it omits header assertions on frappe.puts[-1], masking the missing rollback attribution headers.
findings.reproduce: Inspect tests/unit/test_writeback.py:195-202; run .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_writeback.py -k test_rollback_restores_before_values_once and observe it passes despite rollback sending no audit headers.

findings.finding: The test suite contains zero tests exercising decimal fields in writable_fields or proposal patches.
